rationale: X independently rediscovers both of the GT's heaviest-weighted concerns — the trust_remote_code default flip (author: 'this looks like a bug') and the endpoint-restrictions-resolved-from-wrong-pipeline issue that was the PR's main review thread — with concrete file:line evidence and even flags a plausible residual gap (default deploy/<model_type>.yaml swap not covered by the new test) that the GT thread implies was still being worked out. X's downside is redundancy (the trust_remote_code point is restated three times as separate 'findings'), hurting precision. Y is better organized and finds one good original issue (else-branch skipping UNSUPPORTED_ROUTES) but treats the core pipeline-mismatch issue as fully resolved — an overconfident claim given GT shows this required an explicit author fix — and its 'APPROVE, no blockers' verdict undersells a concern GT treats as a real bug. Neither candidate touches several GT items (mutable-config caching risk, positional-arg signature risk, CI failures, 500-error exposure, batched-completions audit), keeping recall moderate for both.
